ei.title: Theories and Practices of Sports Fandom
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games. If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy. In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams. If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal? What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan? And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team? These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective. From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people. This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team. There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory. Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends. Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation. That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique. These two basic but competing needs can be satisfied through group membership. Sports team supporters are one such group. For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members. This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams. This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs. Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.” This means that you feel successful by associating yourself with others’ success, especially when you are connected to them in some way. This phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for their sports teams. People feel proud when their team wins the game or performs well. Even though a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any immediate benefits, the mere act of watching the game brings them satisfaction. This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong among some passionate supporters that they even identify themselves with their teams. Because of this identification, they often consider criticism toward their team as a personal attack and become violent in extreme cases. However, as long as the behavior of sports fans does not go too far and harm others, cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions. Supporting a team passionately can help people forget about their daily life challenges. It can also have positive effects on our brains. For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal. If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater. So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses. While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people. Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams. When a team competes in their home stadium, their fans gather to watch the game. Typically, the cheers from the home team’s fans are louder than those from the visiting team’s supporters. This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team, as confirmed by a study in 2021. The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches. It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums. It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds. This means that cheering helps the team’s performance to some extent, although it may not be the determining factor. Sports fandom can be analyzed using both evolutionary and social psychological approaches. Through these perspectives, we can understand why people have loyalty and support for their teams. Given that sports fandom has become more and more common in modern times, we should think about our role as fans. We should establish a healthy culture of fandom and seek ways to practice fandom that can have a positive influence on society. Read More The Changing Face of K-Pop Fandom In the past, being a fan of a Korean pop idol typically meant waving colored balloons at concerts and sending gifts. Most fans, often teenagers, admired their idols from a distance. However, over the past three decades, the K-pop fandom culture has evolved dramatically with the development of digital technology. Today, fans actively engage themselves in communication with their idols through social media platforms. They can provide feedback and suggestions, which can have a beneficial influence on their idols. When they see some positive changes in their idols, they feel rewarded for their contribution. In other words, fans have changed from consumers to active participants in the K-pop phenomenon. In addition to this change in their attitudes and roles, today’s fans express their affection in different ways. Instead of showering their idols with material gifts, they organize fundraising and volunteer activities in the name of their idols. For example, fans of a popular idol group have raised funds to support children’s charities. Fans’ efforts not only promote good images of their idols but also foster the value of sharing. This change in fandom culture shows how fans’ interaction with K-pop idols has become more dynamic and meaningful. The new culture brings fans closer to their idols and provides a more inclusive and rewarding experience for them.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: be include → be included: to be + 과거분사(수동태 부정사)
det.analysis:
① might explain ✅ — 관계대명사 that 뒤 조동사 might + 동사원형 explain으로 맞아요.

② everyone has ✅ — everyone은 단수 취급이라 단수 동사 has가 맞아요.

③ be include ❌ — 'want to be ___ somewhere'에서 개인은 어딘가에 '포함되고 싶은' 것이므로 수동태가 필요해요. to be 뒤에는 과거분사가 와서 to be included(포함되다)가 되어야 해요. 동사원형 include는 틀려요 ←정답

④ be satisfied ✅ — 'can be satisfied'는 '충족될 수 있다'는 수동태(be + p.p.)라 맞아요.
det.tip: to be + 과거분사(p.p.) = 수동태 부정사. want to be included = 포함되고 싶다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: fostering → fostered: 등위접속사 and로 이어진 병렬 구조
det.analysis:
① emerged ✅ — 주어 sports fandom에 맞는 과거시제 동사라 맞아요.

② built ~ and fostering ❌ — 등위접속사 and는 같은 형태를 연결해요. 앞에 과거시제 built(쌓았다)가 있으므로 뒤도 과거시제 fostered(길렀다)여야 병렬이 맞아요. fostering(-ing)은 틀려요 ←정답

③ were likely ✅ — 복수 주어 tribes에 맞는 were로 맞아요.

④ has been passed ✅ — 'the instinct ~ has been passed down'은 '전해져 왔다'는 현재완료 수동태라 맞아요.
det.tip: A and B 병렬: 앞이 과거동사(built)면 뒤도 과거동사(fostered)로 맞춰요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: as confirming → as confirmed: 수동의 의미를 담은 분사구문(과거분사)
det.analysis:
① gather ✅ — 복수 주어 fans에 맞는 동사원형 gather라 맞아요.

② louder than ✅ — 'A는 B보다 더 크다'는 비교급 louder than으로 맞아요.

③ as confirming ❌ — 'as ___ by a study'는 '연구에 의해 확인된 바와 같이'라는 뜻이에요. 이 역학이 연구에 의해 '확인되는' 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 confirmed가 맞아요. confirming(능동)은 틀려요 ←정답

④ was found ✅ — 'It was found that ~'은 '~라는 것이 밝혀졌다'는 수동태라 맞아요.
det.tip: (as) + 과거분사 = ~된 대로/~되듯이. as confirmed by ~ = ~에 의해 확인되듯이

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: identical → different: 남과 '다르고' 독특하고 싶어 함
det.analysis:
① inclusion(소속) ✅ — 어딘가에 소속되고 싶은 욕구 문맥에 맞아요.

② identical(똑같은) ❌ — 사람들은 소속되고 싶어 하면서도 남과 '다르고(different)' 독특하고 싶어 해요. identical(똑같은)은 unique(독특한)와 모순되어 틀려요. 원문은 different가 맞아요 ←정답

③ satisfied(충족되는) ✅ — 두 욕구가 집단 소속을 통해 충족된다는 문맥에 맞아요.

④ supporting(응원하는) ✅ — 같은 팀을 응원함으로써 소속 욕구를 충족한다는 문맥에 맞아요.
det.tip: want to be different and unique(다르고 독특하고 싶다)에서 different가 unique와 짝을 이룹니다.

So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses.  While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of ③<u>conflict</u> between people.  Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams.  When a team competes in their home stadium, their fans gather to watch the game. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: conflict → bonding: 옥시토신은 사람 사이의 '유대감'에 기여
det.analysis:
① pleasure(즐거움) ✅ — 도파민이 목표에 도달할 때 즐거움을 느끼게 한다는 문맥에 맞아요.

② greater(더 큰) ✅ — 목표를 오래 추구했을수록 효과가 더 크다는 문맥에 맞아요.

③ conflict(갈등) ❌ — 옥시토신은 사람들 사이의 '유대감(bonding)'에 기여하는 호르몬이에요. conflict(갈등)는 정반대라 틀려요 ←정답

④ louder(더 큰) ✅ — 홈 팬들의 응원이 원정 팬보다 더 크다는 문맥에 맞아요.
det.tip: oxytocin ~ contributes to feelings of bonding(유대감에 기여)에서 bonding이 맞습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: mutual cooperation = 상호 협력(신뢰를 쌓고 관계를 기름)
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에는 무리에서 서로 도우며 무거운 사냥감을 함께 옮겼다는 내용이, 빈칸 뒤에는 '신뢰를 쌓고 관계를 길렀다'는 결과가 나와요. 서로 돕는 행위를 한 단어로 묶으면 상호 협력이에요.

✅ ① mutual cooperation(상호 협력) — 서로 돕는 행위가 신뢰와 관계를 만들었다는 흐름에 딱 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ② personal ambition(개인적 야망) — 함께 돕는 내용과 반대예요.

❌ ③ physical strength(신체적 힘) — 힘이 아니라 협력이 신뢰를 만들었어요.

❌ ④ random luck(우연한 행운) — 본문 단서와 무관해요.
det.tip: help each other in groups(무리에서 서로 도움) → mutual cooperation(상호 협력)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: the determining factor = 결정적인 요인(응원이 도움은 되나 결정 요인은 아님)
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에서 응원이 팀 성적에 '어느 정도' 도움이 된다고 했지만, 그렇다고 성적을 완전히 좌우하는 것은 아니라는 대조가 이어져요. although(비록 ~이지만)이 단서예요.

❌ ① a temporary trend(일시적 유행) — 문맥과 무관해요.

❌ ② an outdated theory(낡은 이론) — 응원 효과와 관련이 없어요.

❌ ③ a minor detail(사소한 세부 사항) — 8% 감소는 사소하지 않아요.

✅ ④ the determining factor(결정적인 요인) — '도움은 되지만 결정적 요인은 아니다'라는 대조에 맞아요 ←정답
det.tip: helps ~ to some extent, although it may not be ~(어느 정도 돕지만 ~은 아닐 수도) 구조로 추론해요.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 생존에 유리한 쪽은 고립된 개인이 아니라 무리의 일원
det.analysis:
❌ ① 일치 — 'sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago'와 같아요.

✅ ② 불일치 — 본문은 'a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual'이라 했어요. 즉 '무리의 일원'이 생존에 더 유리했으므로, '홀로 지내는 개인'이 더 유리했다는 진술은 정반대라 틀려요 ←정답

❌ ③ 일치 — 'People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks'와 같아요.

❌ ④ 일치 — 'tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied'와 같아요.
det.tip: more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual(무리의 일원이 고립된 개인보다 생존 유리)

ch: 진화적 관점에서 스포츠 팬덤은 수만 년 전 부족 수렵채집 조상에게서 비롯되었다.
홀로 지내는 개인이 무리에 속한 사람보다 생존 가능성이 더 높았다.
무리를 이룬 사람들은 어려운 과업을 처리할 때 서로 도울 수 있었다.
공동체 의식이 더 강한 부족이 덜 결속된 부족을 이길 가능성이 높았다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 같은 팀 응원 → 소속 충족 + 독특함도 느낌
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불일치 — 이 이론은 소속(inclusion)과 차별화(differentiation) '둘 다'에 대한 욕구가 있다고 봐요. 소속 욕구만 있다는 것은 틀려요.

❌ ② 불일치 — 본문은 'being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends'라 해서 친구 사귀기와 '다르다'고 했어요.

✅ ③ 일치 — 같은 도시 팀을 응원하면 소속 욕구를 충족하고(satisfy your need for inclusion), 다른 팀 팬과 달라 독특함도 느낀다(make you feel unique)고 했어요 ←정답

❌ ④ 불일치 — 팀의 색과 응원가는 독특함을 '강화한다(is reinforced)'고 했으므로 약화시킨다는 것은 반대예요.
det.tip: satisfy your need for inclusion ~ make you feel unique(소속 충족 + 독특함)를 동시에 언급해요.

ch: 최적 차별성 이론은 사람에게 오직 소속에 대한 욕구만 있다고 본다.
스포츠 팀을 응원하는 것은 그저 친구를 사귀는 것과 완전히 동일하다.
같은 도시의 팀을 응원하면 소속 욕구를 채우면서 동시에 독특함도 느낄 수 있다.
팀의 색과 응원가는 오히려 팬들이 느끼는 독특함을 약화시킨다.

questions.passage: These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective.  From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago.  At that time, a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual.  People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle.  This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members.  In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied.  Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people.  This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team.  There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory.  Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends.  Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation.  That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique.  These two basic but competing needs can be satisfied through group membership.  Sports team supporters are one such group.  For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members.  This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams.  This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs.  Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory. ” This means that you feel successful by associating yourself with others’ success, especially when you are connected to them in some way.  This phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for their sports teams.  People feel proud when their team wins the game or performs well.  Even though a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any immediate benefits, the mere act of watching the game brings them satisfaction.  This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong among some passionate supporters that they even identify themselves with their teams.  Because of this identification, they often consider criticism toward their team as a personal attack and become violent in extreme cases.  However, as long as the behavior of sports fans does not go too far and harm others, cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions.  Supporting a team passionately can help people forget about their daily life challenges.  It can also have positive effects on our brains.  For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine.  Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal.  If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater.  So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses.  While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people.  Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams.  When a team competes in their home stadium, their fans gather to watch the game.  Typically, the cheers from the home team’s fans are louder than those from the visiting team’s supporters.  This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team, as confirmed by a study in 2021.  The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches.  It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums.  It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds.  This means that cheering helps the team’s performance to some extent, although it may not be the determining factor.  Sports fandom can be analyzed using both evolutionary and social psychological approaches.

questions.passage: __________, as confirmed by a study in 2021.  The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches.  It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums.  It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"이 역학은 홈 팀의 경기력에 영향을 미친다."

[ an / dynamic / has / home / impact / of / on / performance / team / the / the / This ] (12단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 이 역학은 홈 팀의 경기력에 영향을 미친다
det.analysis:
'이 역학은 ~ 영향을 미친다'라서 주어 This dynamic + 동사 has로 시작해요.
→ 무엇을? 'have an impact on ~'(~에 영향을 미치다) 구문이라 has an impact on.
→ 무엇에? '홈 팀의 경기력'은 the performance of the home team.
→ 순서: This + dynamic + has + an + impact + on + the + performance + of + the + home + team (12단어)
det.tip: have an impact on + 명사 = ~에 영향을 미치다. the performance of the home team = 홈 팀의 경기력

questions.wa: This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team
accept: This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team

questions.passage: For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, __________ by supporting the same team with other in-group members.  This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams.  This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs.  Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory. ” This means that you feel successful by associating yourself with others’ success, especially when you are connected to them in some way.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"너는 소속에 대한 너의 욕구를 충족할 수 있다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) can, for, inclusion, need, satisfy, you, your 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 너는 소속에 대한 너의 욕구를 충족할 수 있다
det.analysis:
'너는 ~ 충족할 수 있다'라서 주어 you + 조동사 can + 동사원형 satisfy로 시작해요.
→ 무엇을? '너의 욕구'는 your need.
→ 어떤 욕구? '소속에 대한'이니 for inclusion(소속에 대한).
→ 순서: you + can + satisfy + your + need + for + inclusion (7단어)
det.tip: 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형(satisfy). a need for ~ = ~에 대한 욕구

questions.wa: you can satisfy your need for inclusion
accept: you can satisfy your need for inclusion
